description: The Earth Rabbit in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1939 and 1999 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Rabbit is the Rabbit born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the fourth animal. It combines the Rabbit's gentleness with Earth's qualities. Earth Rabbit years between 1924 and 2044 are 1939 and 1999. The Rabbit's fixed element is Wood.

sections.heading: The Earth Rabbit personality
paragraphs: An Earth year gives the Rabbit a practical, settled quality that suits its love of home. In the controlling cycle, Wood controls Earth, and the Rabbit always carries Wood, so here the animal is pictured as working gently on the ground beneath it, like roots holding soil in place. Earth Rabbits are typically described as sensible, thoughtful and materially careful, with a clear idea of the comfortable, secure life they want to build. They often make reliable friends and tactful colleagues who prefer steady progress to bold leaps. That pairing of careful Earth and cautious Rabbit can, however, make them very slow to take risks, and they may stay in an unsatisfying job or arrangement simply because leaving feels unsettling.

Earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind. Descriptions associate it with reliability, honesty and a talent for holding things together, whether that means a family, a budget or a team in a difficult season. Earth-year people are often portrayed as grounded, fair and good at turning ideas into workable plans. The element is linked with nourishment and care, so it carries a quiet generosity. Its shadow, in most readings, is heaviness: worry, stubbornness and a reluctance to move until every risk has been weighed twice.

sections.heading: Earth Rabbit at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

In practical terms, the Earth Rabbit is the reliable diplomat: tactful, organised and sensible with money. Office management, conveyancing, librarianship, mediation and independent retail are frequently suggested, because steady judgement and a pleasant manner build trust there. It prefers stability, transparent processes and a desk where it can work without constant interruption. Within the family, the Earth Rabbit creates a comfortable, orderly home and rarely loses its temper. Loyalty and kept promises are what it values most, and it repays them with years of quiet devotion. The sticking point is caution bordering on inertia: it may postpone difficult conversations, house moves or career changes until the right moment has slipped past unnoticed.

sections.heading: Earth Rabbit years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Earth Rabbit years: 1939, starting Feb 19 and 1999, starting Feb 16. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1939 anyone born before Feb 19 is a Earth Tiger, not a Earth Rabbit. It takes sixty years for the Earth stem and the Rabbit branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Earth Rabbit year is Yin, matching the Rabbit's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Ji-Mao year, the Earth stem Ji with the Rabbit's branch Mao. Births just before each new year fall in the Earth Tiger year (before February 19, 1939) and the Earth Tiger year (before February 16, 1999), and births in the weeks after each Earth Rabbit year ends belong to the Metal Dragon. The new year itself fell on a Sunday in 1939 and Tuesday in 1999.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Rabbit
paragraphs: For Earth Rabbits, confidence tends to grow from evidence, so trying small experiments is more useful than waiting to feel brave. Taking one new class, applying for one stretch role or travelling somewhere unfamiliar can show them how much more they can handle than they assume. Because they often keep worries to themselves, talking plans through with a trusted friend helps them see options clearly. Earth Rabbits also do well with long-term saving or building goals that reward patience. Many readings note that their real security comes from relationships they have quietly tended for years, and remembering that can make change feel less threatening.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Rabbit shares the Rabbit's San He trine with the Goat and Pig (the Wood trine), its Liu He bond with the Dog, and its Liu Chong clash with the Rooster. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Rabbit years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1939 (from February 19, 1939) and 1999 (from February 16, 1999). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Rabbit's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Rabbit's fixed element is Wood; in the five-element cycles wood controls Earth. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Rabbit?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Goat and Pig (San He) and the Dog (Liu He). The Rooster is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Rabbit called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ji-Mao. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Ji, followed by its earthly branch, here Mao for the Rabbit, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Rabbit different from other Rabbits?
faq.answer: All Rabbits share gentleness, tact and refined taste. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
